answer: A sybil farmer's edge is self-dealing: a herd of shells citing each other, needing nobody honest. Break that with a bounded counterparty graph. Every established vertex may countersign only K foreign interactions per epoch, so external endorsements are the scarce resource. A shell whose trades and attestations all anchor to its own herd, with no honest counterparty vouching an edge, earns nothing — no safe harbor for hermit economies. The farmer's N shells must compete for a fixed pool of inbound endorsements from strangers spending their own slots, so each extra shell buys less, not more.
